problem: Prior visual object navigation is category-level: reaching any instance of the target category counts as success. It cannot handle real-life needs that call for a specific instance, described by attributes such as color, material and object references.
motivation: Users usually want one particular instance (e.g. a specific mug), not any object of that category. Instance-level navigation needs instance-level representations that separate same-category objects, and no benchmark for this existed.
key_idea: Introduce the Instance Object Navigation (ION) task and a cascade model: an Instance-Relation Graph navigator whose nodes are instances encoded with color, material and bounding-box location, followed by a grounding module that picks the instance with the highest joint probability of category, color and material.
insight: The abstract only claims that an instance-level graph, rather than a category-level one, helps guide instance navigation and beats the baseline on instance-level metrics. No ablation details are available from the abstract, so the finer reasons are not verifiable.
method: ION task and benchmark: the agent gets instance-level descriptions (color, material, object references) of the target. The AI2-Thor benchmark has over 27,735 automatically generated instance descriptions with navigation ground truth from simulator interaction.
Instance-Relation Graph (IRG): instances are nodes, encoded with color, material and location (bounding box) representations, replacing the category-level graph of earlier work.
Node activation and update: instances detected during navigation activate the corresponding IRG nodes, which are updated by a graph convolutional neural network (GCNN) to guide the navigator.
Instance grounding module: color, material and category regressors with softmax produce a joint probability, and the candidate instance with the maximum probability is chosen as the final prediction.
Cascade framework: the IRG-based navigator and the grounding module run in sequence.

setting.backbone: GCNN over an Instance-Relation Graph, plus category/color/material regressors (details not given in the abstract)
setting.training_data: Self-built AI2-Thor ION benchmark with 27,735 instance descriptions and automatically obtained navigation ground truth
setting.observation: egocentric RGB with detected instances (bounding boxes, colors, materials)

numbers_note: abstract only; no numeric results reported
results: The abstract says the model outperforms the baseline on instance-level metrics on the new AI2-Thor ION benchmark, and that room remains for improvement. No numbers or baseline names are given.
limitations: Evaluated only in the AI2-Thor simulator, with automatically generated descriptions limited to color, material and object references.
The task remains hard, and the authors state there is room for improvement.
builds_on: Category-level graph-based object navigation (e.g., Scene Prior / Graph-based semantic navigation)
